clue.text: Cover for article in transcript

indicators.note: in tells us the article is set inside the word for a transcript

parts.note: a transcript is a copy of something
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone asks how to protect an article that appears in a written record.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy is an overhead covering, such as one over a bed or throne.

clue.text: Girl about to arrive shortly with a complaint

indicators.note: about means the girl's name is wrapped around the short form of arrive

parts.note: Cath is a girl's name, short for Catherine
arr. is the abbreviation for arrive, as on a timetable

explanation.surface: A young woman turns up briefly, bringing an ailment with her.
explanation.definitionFit: Catarrh is a mild ailment, a build-up of mucus in the nose and throat.

clue.text: Tides of siestas across Spain?

indicators.note: across means the naps stretch over either side of the letter for Spain

parts.note: siestas are afternoon naps
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A wry question whether the ebb and flow of Spanish life is measured in siestas.
explanation.definitionFit: Neaps are neap tides, the small-range tides between springs.

clue.text: Mine's support when Dad's about to trip over

indicators.note: about means the word for dad goes around the other letters

parts.note: pop is an informal word for a dad

indicators.note: over suggests the word trip being tipped over, so its letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A father is about to stumble and fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is read as a sign of upset letters, not reversal; 'about' doubles in the surface as part of 'about to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit prop is a timber post holding up the roof of a mine working.

clue.text: Chips — unknown constituents for traditional medication

indicators.note: constituents means the letters of the words are taken as ingredients to be remixed

parts.note: y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Fried potatoes of mysterious composition are offered as an old-fashioned remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Physic is an archaic word for medicine, especially a purgative.

clue.text: Do conservative types sit on them?

definitions.text: Do conservative types sit on them?

parts.words: Do conservative types sit on them?
parts.note: the haunches you squat on, and also old-fashioned conservatives in US politics

explanation.surface: A question about where traditionalists rest themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunkers are the haunches, and the word also names diehard conservatives in American politics.

clue.text: Violent Satchmo put first last

indicators.note: put first last tells us the first part of the name moves to the end

parts.note: Satchmo was the nickname of jazz trumpeter Louis Armstrong

explanation.surface: Instructions to a band to have the famous trumpeter play last.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong-arm tactics are forceful and bullying, using physical violence.

clue.text: Illness caused by gap in rising curve

indicators.note: in places the gap inside the turned curve
rising in a down clue means the word for curve reads upwards

parts.note: an arc is a curve
a hole is a gap

explanation.surface: A medical case blamed on a break in an upward graph.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is a serious bacterial infection of the intestine.

clue.text: Girl kept firm in Adriatic port

indicators.note: kept means the girl's name holds the abbreviation for firm inside it

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name
Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A young woman held her ground in an Italian harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancona is a port city on Italy's Adriatic coast.

clue.text: An artist ran word processing in the right way

indicators.note: processing suggests the words are fed through and come out reworked

explanation.surface: A painter did some typing in a proper manner.
explanation.definitionFit: The strait and narrow is the path of moral rectitude, the proper way to live.

clue.text: Some time after a service one gets rid of data

indicators.note: some signals that only part of the following words is taken, a run of letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Some time after church, someone deletes files.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time' reads as part of 'Some time', but it only dresses the surface; the letters run across 'after a service'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eraser removes marks or, in computing, wipes stored information.

clue.text: Hero did so for rosebay?

parts.note: in Greek legend Hero would call out to her lover, the swimmer Leander
the name she cried was that of her lover, who swam the Hellespont to her

explanation.surface: A legendary heroine behaved in some way for the sake of a shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: Hero is not a brave person but the priestess of the legend, whose cry to her lover would be 'O, Leander!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosebay is another name for the oleander, a flowering evergreen shrub.

clue.text: Make each pick different kind of vegetable

indicators.note: different tells us to make the letters into something else

explanation.surface: An instruction to vary every choice you make.
explanation.definitionFit: A chickpea is a legume eaten as a vegetable, the base of hummus.

clue.text: She cheats to beat the Establishment

parts.note: cons are tricks or swindles
to tan someone is to beat them
CE is the Church of England, the established church

explanation.surface: A woman uses dishonest tricks to get the better of the powers that be.
explanation.definitionFit: Constance is a woman's name, so it stands in for 'she'.

clue.text: Pretend to be an Asian healer

parts.note: to sham is to pretend

explanation.surface: Faking it as an Eastern medicine man.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a spirit healer, originally among the peoples of Siberia.

clue.text: To cadge causes bad odour in the Home Counties

indicators.note: in places the smell inside the region's abbreviation

parts.note: the Home Counties are the counties around London, in the South East, SE
pong is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: Begging gives you a bad name in the commuter belt around London.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge is to live off others, scrounging what you can.

clue.text: Assumed identity with no spare material

indicators.note: material hints at raw stuff to be worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone adopts a disguise with no fabric to spare.
explanation.definitionFit: A persona is the role or character a person puts on for others.

clue.text: Bind by inane church regulation?

indicators.note: regulation implies putting the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Asks whether silly church rules tie people down.
explanation.definitionFit: To enchain is to bind in chains or hold fast.

clue.text: Figure I am in property

indicators.note: in places the contraction inside the word for property

parts.note: an estate is landed property
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: Someone sizing up where they stand in the property market.
explanation.definitionFit: To figure is to calculate roughly, to reckon a value.

clue.text: City den takes the cake

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district
a lair is an animal's den

explanation.surface: A financial district hideout comes out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry cake.

clue.text: Great disaster — one can't somehow get over it

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are muddled into another form

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A catastrophe so large that a person cannot get past it.
explanation.definitionFit: The sinking of the Titanic in 1912 is a byword for a huge catastrophe.

clue.text: UN state spreading infection

indicators.note: spreading has the letters fanning out into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A UN member country passing on a disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus is a bacterial infection causing muscle spasms, also called lockjaw.

clue.text: Credit italic letters as being decisive

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: letters suggests the word's characters are taken apart and set again

explanation.surface: Giving credit for sloping type as a deciding factor.
explanation.definitionFit: A critical moment is a crucial, deciding one.

clue.text: With time one gets out of practice, to be honest

parts.note: rusty describes skills dulled by lack of use

explanation.surface: Over time one loses one's touch, to be frank.
explanation.definitionFit: Trusty means reliable and faithful, so honest in dealing.

clue.text: BBC loses head, which is loose

indicators.note: loses head means the first letter of the nickname is dropped

parts.note: Auntie is an affectionate British nickname for the BBC

explanation.surface: The broadcaster sacks its chief, which is lax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' is the verb here, to set free.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose a knot or a dog is to untie or release it.

clue.text: Block in basic construction

parts.note: the ceremonial block laid at the base of a new building

explanation.surface: A building block used at the most fundamental stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundation stone is the first stone laid, often with ceremony, at the base of a building.

clue.text: Scramble an egg? One is getting past it!

indicators.note: scramble, as with eggs, means mix the letters up

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Cooking breakfast leads to a remark about growing old.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageing means growing older, past one's best.

clue.text: Supporters won't start to provide the cash

indicators.note: won't start means the first letter of the word is missing

parts.note: backers are financial supporters

explanation.surface: Sponsors refuse to begin putting up the money.
explanation.definitionFit: Ackers is British slang for money.
